sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:45

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:45:1
items.html:
It returned to be Mati in Keter, etc., and Lo Mati in Hod: It has already been explained and repeated above that the bestowal of Bina to the vessels of the VAK causes it to be Mati in Keter; and then the posterior of the vessel of Keter rules, withholding every illumination of GAR in the Partzuf, even in the vessel of Hochma, and all the more so in the vessels below it, which receive from the vessel of Hochma. And therefore the illumination of GAR departed from the vessel of Hod, and then the vessel turns her face downward and gives the remainder to Yesod, as above. Except that here, in the matter of the turning of the face of the vessel of Hod, there is also a matter of the refinement of the coarseness of phase one to the aspect of the root, so that the light that emerges has no more than the level of Malchut, as the ARI wrote above, that the level of Malchut clothed in the vessel of Yesod. So that in the matter of the turning of the face of Hod there were two aspects: both the matter of the bestowal of the posterior in the place of the face that had been before this, and the matter of the refinement of the coarseness of phase one, which had ruled in all five ends, from Hesed to Hod; and now Hod refined of its phase one and gave only the level of Malchut to the vessel of Yesod. And the reason for this is that there is no more in the level of phase one than five ends, as above in the words of the ARI.
And now the Sefira of Yesod of ZA has been explained to us. For its vessel is of the aspect of Malchut, and this is because the vessel of Hod of ZA, too, is a vessel of Malchut, as above, and all the more so Yesod, which comes after it — in such a way that all these three vessels, Hod, Yesod and Malchut, are all of them an expansion of the vessel of Malchut alone. And the matter of their expansion is chiefly by the force of that above Hey who descended from the coupling of the ZON of Bina, and from the matter of the light of the posterior that remained from the vessel of Hod after she turned her face by the force of the rule of the posterior of Keter; for these two lights belong to the vessel of Yesod.
So that the vessel of Yesod is the aspect of a vessel of Malchut, and the light in it is a joint one, of judgment and of mercy. For the light of the posterior that remained of the Sefira of Hod after she turned her face is the harshest judgment of all the five ends of ZA, being the vessel of phase four from the time of the first expansion, as above. But at the time when the illumination of GAR of Tifferet reached it, then on the contrary it was considered Hesed, for the illumination of GAR turns everything into Hesed; whereas at the time when the illumination of GAR vanished from her, there remained in her nothing but the quality of judgment alone, and that quality of judgment descended to the vessel of Yesod. And you must know that this was a novelty in the Partzuf, for until now nothing of the quality of judgment had been revealed in the Partzuf in all the five ends; on the contrary, the light of Hassadim of the level of phase one ruled in the whole Partzuf, only sometimes with the illumination of GAR and sometimes without the illumination of GAR, as above. But now the level of the light of Hassadim has already refined from the Sefira of Hod, as above, and there is there nothing but the level of Malchut; and the illumination of GAR, too, has vanished from the Partzuf. Therefore all the force of judgment in the vessel of Hod was revealed, and this remainder descended to the vessel of Yesod. And you find that this force of judgment is a novelty that has now been revealed in the vessel of Yesod.
And therefore all five ends are now discerned as the aspect of five Gvurot, that is, by virtue of the renewal of form that they attained in the vessel of Yesod. So that there are now two aspects: that they are five Hassadim, which are in the five ends from Hesed to Hod; and the second is by virtue of their being five Gvurot, namely in the vessel of Yesod.
However, there is here a further light of the Hey in the vessel of Yesod, that is, what reached it from the coupling of the ZON of Bina, as above, which is a very great light; for from the root of her emanation she is phase two, since she came from the coupling of the ZON of phase two, and afterwards, when she descended together with the light of Hesed to the vessels of the VAK, her level was diminished to phase one, as above. And now that she has reached Yesod, her level was again diminished to the level of Malchut. However, since she is from a coupling of phase two, she is therefore discerned as a light of Hesed, only at a low level; and therefore, from her side, the five ends are again discerned in the aspect of five Hassadim, and they sweeten the above five Gvurot that descended to the vessel of Yesod from the remainder of the light of Hod. And so it has been well explained to us that the light of Yesod is a joint light of Hesed and of judgment, which are called the five Hassadim and the five Gvurot: the five Gvurot are from the remainder of the light of the VAK, and the five Hassadim are from the remainder of the male and female of the vessel of Bina, and they mingle and join together in the vessel of Yesod. And one must remember that all this was done here at the time of, and by reason of, the rule of the posterior of the vessel of Keter.
